title: Injective-tower Roos comparison with normalized integer shifts
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be strict inverse sequences indexed by $n\ge1$ with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and use the cochain/cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $N\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$, choose a cochain complex $X_\bullet$ representing $N$ and a quasi-isomorphism $X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ to a K-injective tower complex whose terms $I^i_\bullet$ are injective tower objects [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Total derived limit $L(N)=R\lim N$ means the functor computed by $\lim I_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], with its termwise integer-shift comparison.

Every transition $I_{n+1}^i\to I_n^i$ is a split epimorphism. Each evaluated complex $I_n$ is K-injective, and the termwise product $\Pi(I)=\prod_n I_n$ represents $\prod_n^D I_n$. Write $h_I=1-s_I$, with $\operatorname{pr}_n s_I=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$ for the actual transition $t_n$. For $C(I)=\operatorname{Cone}(h_I)[-1]$, in coordinates $C(I)^i=\Pi(I)^{i-1}\oplus\Pi(I)^i$ the differential is $d(y,x)=(-dy-h_Ix,dx)$. The natural kernel inclusion
$$\eta_I:\lim_n I_n\longrightarrow C(I),\qquad z\longmapsto(0,(z_n)_n)$$
is a quasi-isomorphism with the actual limit-cone components. Its localized rotated cone triangle identifies the Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit] with first vertex the actual total limit $L(N)$, first arrow the actual product of limit projections, and middle arrow $1-s_I$ on the derived product.

For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, under the termwise product identifications there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\chi_{I,r}:C(I[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}C(I)[r],\qquad(y,x)\longmapsto((-1)^r y,x),\qquad \chi_{I,r}\eta_{I[r]}=\eta_I[r].$$
The inverse has the same coordinate formula. These comparisons are coherent for addition of shifts and identify the cone shift with the total-limit shift on the chosen K-injective representatives, naturally after localization. If $p_I:L(N)\to\prod_n^D I_n$ and $\delta_I:\prod_n^D I_n\to L(N)[1]$ are the transported Roos arrows, $\sigma_r:L(N[r])\to L(N)[r]$ is the termwise limit comparison and $\pi_r:\prod_n^D(I_n[r])\to(\prod_n^D I_n)[r]$ is the canonical product/shift comparison, then
$$\pi_rp_{I[r]}=p_I[r]\sigma_r,\qquad\sigma_r[1]\delta_{I[r]}=(-1)^r\delta_I[r]\pi_r,$$
where the second formula uses the canonical identification of $[1][r]$ with $[r][1]$. Products of arbitrary module sheaves need not be exact. No boundedness or hypothesis on the transitions of the original $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix the chosen $I$ and a degree $i$, and put $J=I^i_\bullet$. For an object $M$ define the prefix tower $E_n(M)$ to have $M$ in levels $1,\ldots,n$, identity transitions there, and zero above $n$. A map $E_n(M)\to J$ is determined by its component $M\to J_n$, the lower components being its composites with the transitions. The map $E_n(J_n)\to E_{n+1}(J_n)$ which is identity through level $n$ and zero above it is monic by levelwise exactness. Extend the map $E_n(J_n)\to J$ corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$ across this monomorphism by the definition of injectivity. The level $n+1$ component of the extension is a map $u_n^i:J_n\to J_{n+1}$, and its tower compatibility says $t_n^iu_n^i=\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$. This proves the claimed splitting in every degree without imposing a condition on the original tower.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), injective-transition paragraph; explicit prefix-tower lifting refinement

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective] to $I$ (reindexing positive levels by $n-1$): each $I_n$ is K-injective in $\mathcal A$. Products of module sheaves are formed sectionwise: the module operations are coordinatewise and the sheaf gluing condition holds in each coordinate, so the sectionwise product has the product universal property. Thus all terms of $P=\Pi(I)$ exist. Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] with the set of positive integers. It states both that this termwise product complex is K-injective and that its image under localization, with the localized projections, is the product in $D(\mathcal A)$. No assertion about products of arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms is used.

proof.text: The maps $t_n$ commute with the differentials, so $s$ defined by $\mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ is a chain map and $h=1-s$ is a chain map. The universal property of the product identifies $\ker h^i$ with compatible families, hence with $(\lim I_n)^i$; the differential restricts to the termwise limit differential. For completeness $h^i$ has a section as a sheaf morphism: choose the splittings $u_n^i$ from step 1, set $a_1=0:P^i\to I_1^i$, and recursively set $a_{n+1}=u_n^i(a_n-\mathrm{pr}_n)$. Then $a_n-t_n^ia_{n+1}=\mathrm{pr}_n$. The product map $a=(a_n)_n:P^i\to P^i$ therefore satisfies $h^ia=\mathrm{id}_{P^i}$. In particular $0\to\lim I_n\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{h}P\to0$ is degreewise short exact. The sections need not commute with the differential; only their degreewise existence has been used.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), short exact product sequence; explicit split recursion

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] with both complexes equal to $P$ and $f=h$. Step 3 verifies its degreewise epimorphism hypothesis and identifies its kernel with the actual termwise limit. Its displayed differential is exactly $d(y,x)=(-dy-hx,dx)$, and its comparison has components $(0,j)$. Therefore it gives the specified $\eta_I$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism with a cone, and proves that $\eta_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The actual limit-cone components are $\mathrm{pr}_n j$, so this comparison also retains every specified projection.

proof.text: Use precisely the cone triangle convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $P\xrightarrow{h}P\xrightarrow{\iota}\operatorname{Cone}(h)\xrightarrow{-\operatorname{pr}_2}P[1]$. Its inverse rotation is $C(I)\xrightarrow{\alpha}P\xrightarrow{h}P\xrightarrow{\beta}C(I)[1]$, where $\alpha(y,x)=x$ and $\beta(b)=(b,0)$ after the canonical shift reindexing. Indeed inverse rotation negates the shifted third arrow, cancelling the minus in $-\operatorname{pr}_2$. Localize and replace $QC(I)$ by $Q(\lim I_n)$ using $Q\eta_I$. The first arrow becomes $Qj$, since $\alpha\eta_I=j$, and the second is $Qh=1-s$ on the actual derived product of step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $Q(\lim I_n)$ computes the stated total derived limit on this chosen representative. The resulting distinguished triangle is a Roos triangle in the exact sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. Its boundary is explicitly $\delta_I=(Q\eta_I[1])^{-1}Q\beta$.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), rotation convention as fixed in def-weil-abstract-derived-category; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941

proof.text: Identify $\Pi(I[r])$ with $P[r]$ by the identity on each product projection. It identifies $h_{I[r]}$ with $h_I[r]$. Apply [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-coordinate-calculus] to $(V,s)=(P,h_I)$ and reorder its coordinates $(v,u)$ as $(y,x)=(u,v)$. The resulting comparison is exactly $\chi_{I,r}(y,x)=((-1)^ry,x)$, its inverse has the same formula, and its zero-shift, additive-coherence and naturality assertions apply. Taking its augmentation $J$ to be the inclusion $j:\lim I_n\to P$ gives $\chi_{I,r}\eta_{I[r]}=\eta_I[r]$ under the termwise limit comparison. This comparison is legitimate on the chosen resolutions: $I[r]$ still has injective terms, and is K-injective because a map from an acyclic tower complex into $I[r]$ shifts back to a map from an acyclic tower complex into $I$; shifting a null-homotopy back gives the required null-homotopy. Here acyclicity is preserved by a shift since its cycles and boundaries are merely reindexed, with differentials multiplied by a unit.

source.place: Tag 011G (definition-shift-cochain); derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone); existing endomorphism-fibre coordinate calculation

proof.text: Write $\alpha_I:C(I)\to P$ and $\beta_I:P\to C(I)[1]$ for step 5's maps. Projection onto $x$ gives $\pi_r\alpha_{I[r]}=\alpha_I[r]\chi_{I,r}$. Insertion into the $y$ coordinate gives $\chi_{I,r}[1]\beta_{I[r]}=(-1)^r\beta_I[r]\pi_r$, since both sides send $b$ to $((-1)^rb,0)$. Put $e_I=Q\eta_I$ and use step 6's identity $Q\chi_{I,r}\,e_{I[r]}=e_I[r]\sigma_r$. Substitution into $p_I=Q\alpha_I e_I$ proves $\pi_rp_{I[r]}=p_I[r]\sigma_r$. Substitution into $\delta_I=e_I[1]^{-1}Q\beta_I$ proves $\sigma_r[1]\delta_{I[r]}=(-1)^r\delta_I[r]\pi_r$, by cancelling the isomorphism $e_I[r][1]$. The reindexings identify $[1][r]$ with $[r][1]$ as stipulated. Thus the boundary sign is computed on its actual insertion map, not inferred from an arbitrary isomorphism of triangles.

proof.text: A strict map $f:I\to I'$ induces the product map $a$, with $ah_I=h_{I'}a$, and the induced limit map $\ell$ satisfies $aj=j'\ell$. The diagonal cone map therefore obeys $C(f)\eta_I=\eta_{I'}\ell$ by [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-coordinate-calculus]. To pass to localization use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] in the abelian tower category: every derived map between the chosen K-injectives has a chain representative unique up to tower homotopy, and a quasi-isomorphism between them is a homotopy equivalence. The cone maps respect these homotopies by [lem-pur-strict-roos-homotopy-functor]. Termwise limit also respects a tower homotopy: its compatible component homotopies restrict from the product to the limit, and $f-g=dH+Hd$ restricts to the same identity there. Consequently the comparisons and the two arrow identities above are natural after localization. A change of K-injective representative is transported through its homotopy equivalence, and the chain identities survive that transport. The termwise limit shift here is exactly the normalized shift comparison used to compute $L$, while step 6 gives coherence for all successive shifts. This proves all claimed naturality and shift-coherence clauses.

tool_uses.why: Evaluation of a K-injective tower is K-injective for a general abelian category; the compatibility unit has no replacement for this exact-adjoint tool.
Termwise products of K-injectives represent derived products without exactness of products; this is a generic homological algebra tool.
The specified zero-first-coordinate kernel inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism for a degreewise epi; this generic cone lemma supplies the chain-level normalization.
Identifies termwise limit on the chosen K-injective tower with the total derived-limit functor whose normalization this item refines.
Generic signed fibre/shift and augmentation identities, with no coefficient or product-exactness assumptions, supply the cone coordinate calculation.
